title: Evaluation and observability: project 2
why: A measured evaluation story is the single strongest differentiator on a junior CV, and most candidates skip it. This is where careful measurement becomes your edge.
outcomes: Build a golden dataset, including unanswerable questions
Use an LLM judge and check it against your own labels
Trace cost and latency, and run evals in CI
lessons: Write 40 golden questions with expected sources, 10 of them unanswerable
Measure retrieval: hit rate and recall at k
Measure generation: faithfulness and answer relevancy with RAGAS or an LLM judge
Hand-label 20 answers and check the judge agrees with you
Add tracing with LangSmith or Langfuse; log cost and latency per request
Run one experiment (chunk size or k), record before and after, add evals to CI
resources: About two hours on tracing, evaluators and improving an agent step by step, with notebooks.
method: Look at your data. Read 50 real outputs before trusting any metric, write down the failure types you see, and make sure your metrics count those failures.
build: Project 2: an evaluation harness with a results table, one documented experiment and evals running in CI.

proj.about: An evaluation harness for your RAG app: a set of test questions with known answers, scores for retrieval and for answers, an LLM judge you've checked against your own marks, and tracing for cost and speed. One documented experiment shows a change that made it measurably better.
skills: Retrieval metrics (hit rate, recall at k)
Judging answers and checking the judge
proj.market: Adverts ask for monitoring, observability and responsible AI. Few junior candidates can show measured results, so this is where you stand out.

worked.t: Mini eval: score the mini RAG
worked.intro: Measure the mini RAG from project 1's worked example with a golden set, a retrieval metric and a simple judge. The same shape scales to your real project.

steps.md:
```py
GOLD = [
    {"q": "How many leave days carry over?", "src": {"leave-p3"}, "answer": "Five days."},
    {"q": "Deadline for carried-over leave?", "src": {"leave-p4"}, "answer": "31 March."},
    {"q": "Do I need a receipt for £80 of expenses?", "src": {"expenses-p2"}, "answer": "Yes, and approval."},
    {"q": "What's the canteen menu?", "src": set(), "answer": None},
]
```

The last one has no source: the right behaviour is to refuse.

```py
def hit_rate(k=2):
    answerable = [g for g in GOLD if g["src"]]
    hits = sum(1 for g in answerable if g["src"] & {d for d, _ in retrieve(g["q"], k)})
    return hits / len(answerable)

print("hit rate @2:", hit_rate())
```

Run it, change the chunking or the threshold, and run it again. That's an experiment.

```py
def judge(question, reference, reply):
    msg = client.messages.create(model="claude-haiku-4-5", max_tokens=5,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Reference: {reference}\nReply: {reply}\nDoes the reply agree with the reference? Answer PASS or FAIL."}])
    return msg.content[0].text.strip().upper().startswith("PASS")
```

Mark the four replies yourself first, then compare with `judge`. If you disagree on more than one, tighten the judge's wording.

```py
refused = answer(GOLD[3]["q"]).startswith("I can't find")
print("refuses unanswerable:", refused)
```

A wrong, confident answer to an unanswerable question is the worst failure, so track it separately.

- 30 to 50 questions, at least five unanswerable.
- Hit rate and recall at 5, plus correct and faithful rates.
- Check the judge against 20 answers you marked by hand.
- Trace each request (chunks, tokens, time, cost).
- One write-up: what you changed, what you held constant, before and after numbers.
- A CI job that fails if hit rate drops more than five points.
